notes: Category 3 of the taxonomy in docs/pool_edge_plan.md: the interval contains both zero AND the hypothesised effect, so the test said nothing. These are NOT negatives.
The evaluator resolves ~2 ATS points (RWB-15). Most single features are worth a fraction of that, so landing here is the DEFAULT outcome for a real small signal.
Effects are stored so POSITIVE FAVOURS THE CANDIDATE regardless of the metric's own polarity; Brier and MAE must be negated before recording.
A pooled estimate justifies ONE predeclared combined look on a rotation window none of the inputs touched. It is never itself a finding.

best_pick_opener_ranker_dispersion_filte.classification_evidence: Head-to-head audit of the open registry lead (best_pick_opener_ranker_dispersion_filtered_candidate_vs_unfiltered, +3.92 pts vs its UNFILTERED parent, P+ 0.813) against the ACTUAL live production v2 nomination rule (nfl_ats.best_pick_nomination.select_nominee: same filter, dispersion tie-break within the pool) rather than that unfiltered baseline. Survives the tie-break audit (tie-agnostic recompute moves the original lead from +3.92 to +3.43 pts, P+ 0.813 to 0.798 -- not a majority-tie artifact like sweep_robustness' collapsed +8.68). The head-to-head interval's lower bound is exactly 0.0, but per this registry's schema there is no 'confirmed positive' classification (only unresolved_below_power / refuted_mechanism / bounded_by_control), and wrong_sign_resolved requires the interval on the NEGATIVE side, which does not apply to a non-negative lean -- unresolved_below_power is the only admissible classification. IMPORTANT CAVEAT the notes field expands on: the entire +0.97-point estimate traces to exactly ONE of 103 paired weeks (2023 week 15) where the two rules' nominees differ AND settle differently; a second nominally-diverging week (2020 week 8) produced identical lift for both rules and contributes zero net difference. This is an N=1 result wearing a P+ of 0.631 -- an EV-positive forced-pick lean per AGENTS.md, not a resolution, and reported as such.

Neither meets a closing ground: no resolved wrong sign (interval not entirely negative) and split-half reliability of the new value-weighted trait is confidently POSITIVE not indistinguishable from zero (dropback SB=0.033 P+=0.958, carry SB=0.049 P+=0.986; averaged to 0.041 for this field) -- far below the plain cfb_role_continuity trait's own 0.719/0.680, so the refuted_mechanism reliability route is also unavailable. cfb_value_weighted_role_continuity.notes: Predeclared only as a scratchpad DRAFT (rapm_scope/predeclaration_draft.md + implementation_plan.md), never frozen into docs/; reframed from RAPM (not buildable on CFB's credited-actor-only data) to value-weighted role continuity. VALUE_RELIABILITY_PRIOR_PLAYS=500 / VALUE_EPA_CLIP=5.0 mirrored verbatim from NFL participation.py -- EXPLICITLY UNDERIVED for CFB's play volume/EPA distribution (adjudicated decision 5). Weight formula 'state x value_rate' is an inferred reading of an ambiguity the adjudication did not resolve (see results.md deviation 2). Mechanically flagged: ~50.7% of team-game rows fall back to neutral via active_mass sign-cancellation (45.1% of qualifying player-games have negative value_rate), and the non-neutral continuity tail is unbounded (dropback [-286.9,+233.7], carry [-40.3,+343.2]) -- a likely instrument-design defect in the literal weight formula, not just a power limit; a rectified weight was not tried (would be a new, undeclared family). Source: scripts/cfb_value_weighted_continuity_screen.py, artifacts/cfb_value_weighted_continuity/20260818T211758Z/. Reviewer note 2026-08-18: the actionable finding is the instrument defect, not the effect -- the state-times-value_rate weight cancels ~50.7% of team-game rows to neutral via sign cancellation and has unbounded tails (dropback [-287, +234]); split-half reliability 0.033-0.049 is confidently positive but ~5-15% of the plain trait's 0.68-0.72. Any successor should redesign the weight (e.g. magnitude-based) before re-screening; this entry prices the tested formula only.

estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.classification_evidence: Own-model pick stability: single-fit pairwise flip rate (two individual bootstrap-refit draws disagreeing) 26.4% vs bagged split-half flip rate (mean of first 60 vs mean of second 60 of 120 refit draws disagreeing) 4.5% -- a 5.9x reduction, on 8,933 CFB games / 13 seasons. Accuracy: single-fit 51.14% vs bagged 51.31% (+0.17 pts, bagging beats the single fit). Bagged-vs-baseline (full-vs-thin) paired comparison: -0.168 acc pts [naive interval], P+ 0.383 (up from the single-fit arm's -0.336 pts / P+ 0.262 -- still crosses zero, so unresolved, but a genuine partial improvement in both estimate and P+ relative to not bagging). A DIRECT synthetic falsification attempt (fresh-bootstrap-of-a-training-resample own-model-instability design) found a null result instead (single flip 9.5% vs bagged 10.0%); diagnosed as a comparator design flaw (bootstrapping a bootstrap resample compounds variance rather than testing a fair 'fresh draw of history'), not evidence against the real-data finding. The real-data split-half design (splitting one clean bootstrap ensemble in half, no nested resampling) is the trustworthy comparator.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.description: Average predicted centres over training-row bootstrap-refit draws (bagging) instead of reporting a single point-estimate fit. Screened on the CFB thin-vs-full candidate comparison, reusing the refit draws already computed for the honest interval -- no extra fitting.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.notes: The flip-rate reduction (pick stability) is the strong, decisive part of this result; the accuracy/P+ improvement is real but modest and does not clear any promotion bar on its own. Recommend bagging as a default variance-reduction step for FUTURE candidate screens (it cannot move any current pick since it is not wired into any production path), not as a standalone accuracy claim. CORRECTION (recording agent, 2026-08-18): the drafted payload this entry is sourced from recorded effect=+0.17, which is sign-inconsistent with its own probability_positive=0.3825 and its own classification_evidence text ('-0.168 acc pts ... P+ 0.383'); +0.17 was actually the SEPARATE bagged-vs-single-fit accuracy delta (51.31% vs 51.14%), not the bagged-vs-baseline comparison this P+ describes. Recorded here as effect=-0.168 to match docs/estimation_variance.md sec 4a's literal 'Bagged vs. baseline, naive interval | -0.17 pts [naive], P+ 0.383' under this registry's positive-favours-candidate convention. The underlying finding (bagging helps, relative to the single fit) is unchanged by this correction; only the sign of the recorded full-vs-thin effect number is fixed.

estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.classification_evidence: Non-monotonic and noisy: shrink_fraction=1.0 (production strength) gives -0.336 acc pts, P+ 0.255; 0.75 -> -0.448 pts P+ 0.181; 0.5 -> -0.414 pts P+ 0.208; 0.25 -> +0.034 pts P+ 0.543 (essentially zero, not a real flip, just the least-negative point); 0.0 -> -1.209 pts P+ 0.041. A matched synthetic check (linear DGP, location-biased residual sample, 100 replicates x n_boot=50) found the OPPOSITE, clean, monotonic pattern instead: shrink=1.0 always best (+1.67 pts, P+ 0.707), declining smoothly to shrink=0 (-5.52 pts, P+ 0.091). Flip-rate DOES fall monotonically with shrinkage in both the real and synthetic data (confirms the mechanism -- production's cover probability threshold is fixed against a nonzero-location residual sample, so uniform positive scaling is NOT sign-invariant, unlike coefficient scaling closed by MOD-06), but the real-data accuracy/P+ sweep does not replicate the synthetic monotonic decline, so there is no basis to claim a shrinkage sweet spot exists.
estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.description: Uniformly shrinking the predicted market-residual CENTRE (not the residual-sample READER, which residual_location.md already found inert) toward the market line by a fraction before reading the out-of-time residual ECDF. Screened on the thin-vs-full CFB comparison (market/context/experience-only baseline vs full CFB_MODEL_FEATURE_COLUMNS candidate).
estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.notes: Do not treat shrink=0.25's near-zero, barely-positive point estimate as a discovery -- it is the least-bad of five noisy negative-leaning arms, not a validated improvement. Recorded per AGENTS.md's binding rule (every category-3 result recorded, not discarded) precisely because it crosses zero, not because it looks promising. Recorded 2026-08-18 by a recording agent from docs/estimation_variance.md sec 4b/sec 6 (the drafting session was barred from writing registry/*.json; this session verified the doc's numbers against sec 4b's table before recording, no fields required derivation).

estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.classification_evidence: Ungated (tau=0): -0.336 acc pts, P+ 0.264 (candidate LOSES to baseline). Gated at tau=0.05 (defer to baseline wherever the two arms' cover probabilities differ by <5 points): +0.246 acc pts, P+ 0.9505, f falls 19.8% -> 2.06% (MDE80 1.32 -> 0.43 pts). The sign flip and P+ jump REPLICATE independently on two disjoint season halves built by alternating clean-core seasons (scripts/estvar_f_lever_splithalf.py): half A (2012/14/16/18/21/23/25) P+ 0.399 -> 0.935 at tau 0->0.05; half B (2013/15/17/19/22/24) P+ 0.241 -> 0.744 at tau 0->0.05. Recorded unresolved rather than resolved because tau=0.05 was chosen from a 9-point sweep AFTER seeing the pooled result -- the split-half check supports the QUALITATIVE pattern (a modest disagreement gate makes this comparison provable) but not the specific tau or P+ figure at full precision; a predeclared tau on a train/validation split, confirmed once on a held-out test split, is required before this could be called resolved.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.description: Gate the 'full' CFB feature profile's influence to games where its predicted cover probability disagrees with the 'thin' (market+context+experience only) baseline by at least tau, deferring to the baseline elsewhere. Tests the general 'f lever' principle (MDE80 = 280*sqrt(f/n)): a surgical candidate that only moves the picks it has real information about is more provable than one that perturbs every pick.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.notes: This is a DETECTION-METHOD finding, not a new predictive feature -- 'full' and 'thin' are both already-existing profiles. The actionable implication is a general design principle for evaluating future candidates (gate influence to where the candidate disagrees with a simpler baseline), not a pick change. Do not promote or apply to any live model; this only screens the evaluator's own sensitivity. Recorded 2026-08-18 by a recording agent from docs/estimation_variance.md sec 5/sec 6 (the drafting session was barred from writing registry/*.json; this session verified the doc's tau=0.05 row and split-half table before recording, no fields required derivation).

estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.classification_evidence: Out-of-screen population (thin_2006_2011 minus 2006-2007, which fall below the 500-game training floor entirely under annual-refit cadence, + regime_2020): 2,533 games, 72 blocks. Real gate (tau=0.05, frozen, not re-swept): -0.316 acc pts, honest 95% interval [-1.323, +0.699] (refit_aware_interval, samples=20000), honest P+ 0.2733 -- crosses zero, does NOT directionally replicate clean-core's positive lean (P+ 0.9505 pooled, 0.935/0.744 split-half). Required placebo control (random gate, same n=411 membership count, seed 20260818): -0.553 acc pts, P+ 0.0512 -- worse than the real gate, which is evidence the disagreement selection is not arbitrary even though neither arm beats baseline here. Gate-membership reliability (120 paired refit draws): 23.09% overall flip rate under training-row resampling (1 - flip rate = 0.7691 recorded as reliability, converted to the registry's higher-is-better convention), 32.82% among point-fit in-gate games, 21.20% among out-gate games -- real instability, not enough alone to close as no_split_half_reliability. Realized f (7.03%) and membership rate (16.23%) are far above clean-core's ~2%, consistent with the flagged sparser-market regime confound (2a caveat 2) and not separable from it in this design. MDE80 at realized f/n is 1.47 pts, worse than the design's own 0.69-pt a-priori estimate and ~6x the original screen's +0.246-pt effect -- underpowered as expected, and the honest read is directional, not resolving, and leans negative rather than positive.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.description: Out-of-screen retrospective confirmation of the tau=0.05 f-lever disagreement gate (gate the CFB full profile's influence to games where it disagrees with the thin profile by >=0.05, deferring to thin elsewhere), frozen before this run per flever_scope/design.md. Tested against a required size-matched random-gate placebo control.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.notes: Confirmation run per flever_scope/design.md (2026-08-18), orchestrator adjudication: CFB-only (no NFL window drawn), no P+ bar applied to this methodology question, placebo arm required and run. Does NOT resolve or refute the disagreement-gate mechanism; the honest single-population read here is more cautionary than the design's hoped-for outcome (directional replication) -- point estimate and P+ both lean the WRONG way relative to clean-core on this specific out-of-screen population, though not to a resolved degree. The real-vs-placebo gap is the one piece of this run that leans toward the mechanism being non-arbitrary. Do not promote or apply to any live model.

hc_year_one_fade.classification_evidence: Era split is the whole question: clean 2009-2017 gap is +0.09 (n=391), mined 2018-2025 gap is -8.08 (n=465). The clean era REFUTES the -8 magnitude but NOT a moderate true effect -- a true -4 sits only 1.43 sigma from the clean-era observation, so it is not excluded. An earlier draft of this session called that a category-2 close; that was wrong and is corrected here. Escapes the closed coach-quality-reputation mechanism (reliability 0.063), which is a claim about a persistent coach TRAIT; this is an event/transition claim needing no stable trait. Not the team-quality ceiling either: invariant to quality by construction, and the gap survives inside the low-quality tercile (45.75% vs 51.46%).
hc_year_one_fade.description: First-year head coaches, weeks 1-8, cover below the kept-coach rate. Reproduced by two independent pipelines: 46.73% year-one vs 50.99% kept-coach on 856 games, gap -4.26 points.
hc_year_one_fade.notes: SCALE: the raw effect is a 4.26-point cover-rate gap on the 783 games (17.7% of the slate) with a first-year coach in weeks 1-8. Recorded on the FULL-SLATE scale so it is commensurable with feature-level accuracy deltas; an un-scaled subset effect would dominate any pool it entered. SIGN: the raw gap is negative (year-one coaches cover less); recorded positive because the registry's sign asks whether the evidence favours the candidate HYPOTHESIS, which was exactly that they underperform. SIGN ORIENTATION: the raw cover-rate gap is -4.26 (year-one coaches cover LESS). Recorded as +4.26 because the registry's sign asks whether the evidence favours the CANDIDATE HYPOTHESIS, and the hypothesis was exactly that they underperform -- the edge is exploitable by fading them. injury_value_lost_gradient.classification_evidence: Unchanged headline: the disagreement statistic resolves (rank-biserial +0.248 [+0.046,+0.450], p=0.016) but the ACCURACY effect does not (+1.75 [-0.69,+4.27], P+ 0.899) on the already-spent [2020, 2021] window, 456 games. NEW this session (docs/injury_value_lost.md): (1) split-half reliability of the underlying value-lost signal, measured on the full 2009-2025 history (4,431 games, 384 team-seasons, temporal odd/even-week split) is Pearson r=0.874 [0.843,0.901], Spearman-Brown corrected full-length reliability=0.933 [0.915,0.948], P+=1.000 (4000/4000 bootstrap draws) -- rules out 'refuted: no split-half reliability' per AGENTS.md. (2) The RAPM-participation value-lost construct (M6, the family's one same-kind negative, -0.43 pts) has EQUALLY high reliability (0.860 raw / 0.925 corrected) -- so reliability does NOT explain M6's negative sign; more likely M6 tests the marginal value of a second, QB-inclusive, correlated value-lost construct stacked on top of one already in the model (full_player_participation = full_player_value + participation family), not whether value-lost as a concept works. (3) The mechanism-screen result survives a market-line-movement control unchanged (value_magnitude vs |close-open| line move: Pearson 0.029, near-zero; residualized disagreement rank-biserial 0.249 [0.047,0.451] p=0.016, statistically identical to the raw 0.248). (4) Survives dropping every QB-involved game: on the 397/456 games (87%) where neither presumed starter carried any listed injury, rank-biserial is still positive (+0.188 [-0.027,0.403], p=0.086) at comparable magnitude to the full sample -- consistent with the structural code finding that injury_skill_epa_value_lost deliberately zeroes QB rushing/receiving production (players.py:1260-1283), so this is provably not a QB proxy. (5) A methodologically CLEANER isolation exists and was run for the first time: player_value profile on game_features_player_value.parquet (built with FIXED-prior severity per its manifest player_feature_version=v2 tag, confirmed NOT learned) contrasted against the player baseline differs by ONLY the two value-lost columns -- zero semantics-shift confound, unlike this entry's original B-A contrast which mixed learned-severity semantics_shift into the same delta. That clean contrast gives +1.316 pts [-0.460,+3.247], P+ 0.8875, on the same 456 games, 26 disagreements (61.5% candidate win rate) -- smaller than +1.75 (removing the confound costs about a third of a point) but directionally intact. Recommend citing +1.316/P+0.8875 as the number to predeclare a narrowed family against, not the conflated +1.75 recorded here.
injury_value_lost_gradient.description: The availability/player-value half of the MOD-07 stack, whose gain concentrates in games with more injury VALUE lost rather than more availability-RATE shift. Tercile accuracy by value lost is monotone: -0.66 / +0.66 / +5.26 points.
injury_value_lost_gradient.notes: The narrowed candidate worth building: value-weighted injury magnitude with the learned-rate half dropped -- confirmed in docs/injury_value_lost.md section 4 using game_features_player_value.parquet (fixed severity) rather than the weak_stack table (learned severity), which removes the semantics-shift confound entirely. Predeclare as a new family `injury_value_lost_narrowed` inheriting mod07_weak_signal_stack (contaminates [2020,2021]); earliest eligible block after inherited contamination is [2022, 2023], one of only two remaining full opener blocks in the 2020-2025 pool. Do not assign until the 2026 prospective mod07_weak_signal_stack challenger (already ACTIVE_PROSPECTIVE, artifacts/prospective/challengers.json) has produced its own number -- docs/injury_value_lost.md section 7 has the full predeclaration text to freeze verbatim. CFB cannot screen this family: value_lost requires a pregame injury-severity signal and none exists in any CFB source (docs/cfb_data.md, 'Availability semantics (fail closed)'); the nearest feasible CFB proxy (realized participation continuity, a different, postgame construct) already ran and lost (-0.67 pts on 8,933 games, cfb_role_continuity family, closed_negative).

injury_value_lost_prior_week_report.description: D-A contrast rebuilt with a synthetic injuries table keyed at the current week but built only from last week's Friday-final official designation, kept for players who recorded zero snaps in that prior game (report resolved by playing normally is dropped). Tests whether a one-week-lagged, fully Tuesday-visible injury report carries value-lost signal.
injury_value_lost_prior_week_report.notes: Free re-read of the already-spent mod07_weak_signal_stack [2020,2021] window; same 456 games, same D-A methodology (profile=player vs profile=player_value, ridge alpha 10) as injury_value_lost_narrowed. Saturday reproduction check on the same run: +1.3158 pts / P+ 0.8893 (recorded +1.316/0.8875). Reliability of the underlying value-lost trait (0.87-0.93) was established on injury_value_lost_gradient's same-week construction, NOT independently re-measured for this one-week-lagged construction -- left null here, not inherited. DO-NOT-POOL: shares the 456-game [2020,2021] window with injury_value_lost_gradient, injury_value_lost_narrowed, injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_official, injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_augmented, mod07_opener_bias_ablation. Companion arms: injury_value_lost_prior_week_absence (same window, different population); injury_value_lost_prior_week_report_saturday_channel (paired channel-delta vs the same fresh Saturday rebuild). Coverage: 576/9804 team-games (5.9%) are week 1 with no prior week, contributing zero synthetic injury rows in either direction by construction. 76,782 Friday-final report rows; 40,837 dropped as resolved (player recorded snaps in that prior game); 35,945 carried forward as unresolved, 34,494 of which map onto a current-week game with a valid prior week.

injury_value_lost_prior_week_report_satu.classification_evidence: Interval [-1.559, +4.478] crosses zero -- not a resolved wrong sign. No positive-control bound was run. P+ 0.8228 favors Saturday's channel being larger than the prior-week-report channel, i.e. most of the Saturday edge is NOT recovered by this lagged substitute, but the interval crossing zero means this is not a closed/resolved result; stays unresolved_below_power.
injury_value_lost_prior_week_report_satu.description: Paired channel-delta, same 456 games: fresh Saturday-cutoff (real, current-week injuries) D-A minus injury_value_lost_prior_week_report D-A. Isolates how much of the Saturday-cutoff edge a fully Tuesday-visible, one-week-lagged official-report substitute recovers.
injury_value_lost_prior_week_report_satu.notes: Diagnostic companion to injury_value_lost_prior_week_report, same technique injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_channel_official_only used for the Tuesday-official arm (which measured channel_delta +1.3158 pts, P+ 0.9003 -- this prior-week channel is comparably sized at +1.5351 pts but with a lower P+ 0.8228, i.e. less confidently distinguished from zero). Saturday arm in this run reproduced the recorded +1.316/P+0.8875 as +1.3158/P+0.8893. DO-NOT-POOL: shares the 456-game [2020,2021] window with the full injury_value_lost family (see injury_value_lost_prior_week_report's notes for the full list).

injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_officia.classification_evidence: Interval [-0.877, +0.875] crosses zero (expected at this evaluator's resolution per AGENTS.md) and the point estimate itself is exactly 0.0, not a resolved wrong sign (whole interval must sit below zero for wrong_sign_resolved, which this does not). No positive-control bound was run at this cutoff. Stays unresolved_below_power.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_officia.description: injury_value_lost_narrowed D-A contrast (player_value minus player profile, game_features_player_value.parquet construction) rebuilt with a true own-week Tuesday-noon-ET decision cutoff instead of decision_hours_before_kickoff=24 (Saturday), using ONLY the official injury report's own date_modified (no PFT augmentation). Free re-read on the already-spent mod07_weak_signal_stack [2020,2021] opener window, scripts/injury_tuesday_cutoff_experiment.py.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_officia.notes: Only 328/76784 (0.43%) of official injury-report rows have date_modified at or before their own game's Tuesday-noon-ET cutoff (coverage.official_rows_visible_by_tuesday_noon in the result artifact) -- the official report is structurally the wrong instrument for a Tuesday lock (NFL's first weekly practice report files Wednesday). DO-NOT-POOL: shares the 456-game [2020,2021] window with injury_value_lost_gradient, injury_value_lost_narrowed, mod07_opener_bias_ablation. Companion arm: injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_augmented. Reliability of the underlying value-lost trait (0.87-0.93) was established on injury_value_lost_gradient, not independently re-measured for this Tuesday-cutoff construction.

injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_aug.classification_evidence: Point estimate is negative but the interval [-1.129, +0.668] crosses zero -- not a resolved wrong sign (requires the WHOLE interval below zero). No positive-control bound was run at this cutoff. Stays unresolved_below_power; the negative point estimate is reported, not treated as a rejection.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_aug.description: injury_value_lost_narrowed D-A contrast rebuilt with a true own-week Tuesday-noon-ET decision cutoff, injuries table augmented: a designation is treated as visible if either its own date_modified is at/before Tuesday noon OR a ProFootballTalk injury-relevant headline (299,739-URL archive, data/raw/injury_news) names that player, dated at/before that same Tuesday noon (conservative full-name substring match, precision-favoring). Free re-read on the already-spent mod07_weak_signal_stack [2020,2021] opener window.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_aug.notes: PFT augmentation raises visible-row share from 0.43% (official-only) to 8.13% (coverage.pft_augmented_rows_visible_share, 5918 additional rows), still leaving 91.9% of designations unseen by Tuesday noon. DO-NOT-POOL: shares the 456-game [2020,2021] window with injury_value_lost_gradient, injury_value_lost_narrowed, mod07_opener_bias_ablation, and injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_official. Matching is a lower bound (undercounts last-name-only headlines), so this is the more-informed of the two Tuesday arms but still conservative toward finding pre-Tuesday visibility.

injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_chann.classification_evidence: Interval [-0.454, +3.185] crosses zero -- expected at this evaluator's resolution, not grounds to close. Point estimate equals the ENTIRE Saturday D-A effect (1.3158 of 1.3158 pts), i.e. essentially 100% of the measured edge is attributable to information arriving after Tuesday noon under this operationalization. Not a resolved wrong sign, no positive control run; unresolved_below_power.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_chann.description: Paired delta isolating the Tuesday-noon-to-Saturday information channel: (Saturday-cutoff D-A) minus (Tuesday-official-cutoff D-A), same 456 games, week-blocked. Answers whether the injury_value_lost_narrowed backtest edge is actually available to a pool pick locked at Tuesday noon, or draws on information that only exists by Saturday.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_chann.notes: Companion: injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_channel_pft_augmented (+1.535 pts, uses the more complete PFT-augmented Tuesday arm). DO-NOT-POOL with injury_value_lost_gradient/injury_value_lost_narrowed/mod07_opener_bias_ablation/the two injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_* entries -- all share the same 456-game [2020,2021] window. Decision-relevant reading: the pool grades against the Tuesday opener, so this channel is NOT currently harvestable by a forced Tuesday pick even though it is real information value in the Saturday-cutoff backtest.

injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_chann.classification_evidence: Interval [-0.445, +3.672] crosses zero -- expected at this resolution, not grounds to close. Point estimate slightly EXCEEDS the full Saturday effect because the PFT-augmented Tuesday arm's own D-A point estimate is negative (-0.219), so even after crediting Tuesday noon with everything PFT news could foreshadow, the measured Tuesday-locked edge is not just absent but slightly negative in this sample. Not a resolved wrong sign (interval still crosses zero) and no positive control was run; unresolved_below_power.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_chann.description: Paired delta isolating the Tuesday-noon-to-Saturday information channel using the PFT-augmented Tuesday arm: (Saturday-cutoff D-A) minus (Tuesday+PFT-cutoff D-A), same 456 games, week-blocked. Primary/most-informed operationalization of the two channel-delta entries.
injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_chann.notes: Companion: injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_channel_official_only (+1.316 pts, official-report-only Tuesday arm). DO-NOT-POOL with injury_value_lost_gradient/injury_value_lost_narrowed/mod07_opener_bias_ablation/injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_official/injury_value_lost_tuesday_cutoff_pft_augmented/injury_value_lost_tuesday_saturday_channel_official_only -- all share the same 456-game [2020,2021] window, a single look decomposed many ways. Decision-relevant reading: forced picks, pool grades at the Tuesday opener -- P+ 0.917 that essentially all (and possibly slightly more than all) of the Saturday-cutoff backtest's measured edge lives in information that does not exist yet at the pool's Tuesday lock. This is the headline number for the pool-relevant question in docs/injury_news_sourcing.md sec 5 exp 1.

movement_direction_tilt_opener.classification_evidence: Interval contains zero at both week- and season-blocking (week-blocked upper bound +0.85 accuracy points, positive), so the whole interval is not on the negative side; wrong_sign_resolved does not apply. Point estimate leans negative (P+ 0.27 week-blocked, 0.23 season-blocked) but that is a lean, not a resolution. No positive-control test was run. Per AGENTS.md taxonomy this is unresolved_below_power.
movement_direction_tilt_opener.description: MOV-01 movement-direction forced-pick tilt, PRIMARY rule: flip the active weak_stack models opener pick to the movement-predicted side only when it disagrees AND predicted-move confidence is in the top half (median-split threshold computed from training-fold in-sample predictions only, never target-season data). Leak-free walk-forward reusing nfl_ats.clv.build_pilot_frame/fit_pilot_model/FROZEN_PILOT_FEATURES with no reimplementation of the model itself: seasons 2021-2023 each get a fresh expanding-window ridge refit trained only on strictly-earlier archived seasons (2021 trained on 2020 only; 2022 trained on 2020-2021; 2023 trained on 2020-2022); seasons 2024 and 2025 reuse the frozen MKT-06 pilot model AS-IS, trained once on 2020-2023 (FROZEN_PILOT_PROTOCOL), with no refit on either target season. Season 2020 excluded: no earlier archived season exists to train a leak-free direction model on. Effect and interval recorded here are OPENER-graded (project primary goal), week-blocked (90 week blocks, primary blocking). Joined population 1310 REG games, 2021-2025, against the active weak_stack opener-evaluation artifact; 59 of 276 opener-pick disagreements passed the confidence gate and were flipped.
movement_direction_tilt_opener.notes: Close-graded secondary read (same opener-anchored decision, settled at the close line via pick_correct(pick_home_at_open, margin_vs_close) -- deliberately NOT the active models own independently re-evaluated close arm, to keep the comparison apples-to-apples): delta -0.23 accuracy points, P+ 0.33 week-blocked / 0.30 season-blocked. Season-blocked bootstrap here uses only 5 blocks (2021-2025 seasons) -- thin, below the ~10-block reliability floor used elsewhere in this repo; read the week-blocked number as authoritative. Companion variants recorded separately: movement_direction_tilt_opener_variant1_no_filter (flip every disagreement) and movement_direction_tilt_opener_variant2_top_quartile (75th-percentile confidence gate).

Effect and interval recorded here are OPENER-graded (project primary goal), week-blocked (90 week blocks, primary blocking). Joined population 1310 REG games, 2021-2025; all 276 opener-pick disagreements were flipped under this rule.

observed_movement_oracle_sunday_am_reali.notes: MERGED recording: the script's sunday_1600_realism (true deadline min(kickoff,16:00 ET)) and sunday_1300_conservative cells in the source CSV are numerically IDENTICAL to 6 decimal places -- measured and verified NOT a bug: every one of the 54 intraday_hourly-covered weeks has its last Sunday-local capture at local hour 10 (zero variance across weeks), i.e. the archive's real coverage ceiling is ~10:55 ET, strictly before both nominal cutoffs, so both resolve to the same last-available capture. offseason_retention_per_metric_cfb.classification_evidence: Week-blocked clean_core interval is entirely below zero (upper -0.199 pts, P+ 0.0037); season-blocked confirms (upper -0.168, P+ 0.0066); the all-seasons superset is tighter still (upper -0.235, P+ 0.0016). Robust to the documented refit-variance correction for feature-construction families (1.003-1.099x, docs/estimation_variance.md Part II): a 10% interval widening leaves clean_core/week entirely below zero. Replicates and sharpens the existing scalar-grid CFB screen (docs/offseason_retention.md): every one of the 8 estimated per-metric values (0.166-0.350) falls inside the range that screen already showed loses to 0.67. Brier/log-loss lean the same direction but do not resolve (P+ 0.032-0.076). thin_2006_2011 and regime_2020 lean the same direction, unresolved, as expected from their lower power.
offseason_retention_per_metric_cfb.description: Per-metric offseason_retention vector (CFB Route-1 season-transition slopes, horizon 4 games, values 0.166-0.350, none clipped) vs the shipped uniform 0.67 scalar, on the frozen XLG-03 CFB benchmark.
offseason_retention_per_metric_cfb.notes: Scope: this refutes THIS candidate construction (CFB Route-1 horizon-4 estimate, clipped [0,1]) at the accuracy metric on the CFB instrument, not per-metric retention as a concept on other instruments. Disclosed caveat: estimation and scoring share the same 2006-2025 CFB corpus; that biases TOWARD the candidate (overfit favours it), so it strengthens rather than weakens this negative. Reviewer adjudication 2026-08-18: terminal verdict accepted -- reopening would require >36% interval widening (upper bound -0.199, centre -0.7475) against the applicable 1.003-1.099x feature-construction correction; the residual_location walk-backs used the reader-family correction, which does not apply to this fit-changing family. Actionable reading: the accuracy-optimal retention on CFB sits at or above 0.67 even though transition slopes measure 0.17-0.35 -- the state features do better carrying MORE prior-season signal than the persistence slopes suggest. DEFAULT_OFFSEASON_RETENTION=0.67 survives its audit.

overlay_stack_combined_opener_2020_2025.classification_evidence: unresolved_below_power, not a terminal closure: the PRIMARY (week-blocked, 107 blocks) interval [-7.478, +1.548] crosses zero (P+ 0.0943 that the combined stack beats the baseline), so wrong_sign_resolved is inadmissible per AGENTS.md ('the wrong sign is a lean, not a resolution' unless the whole interval sits below zero). The season-blocked reading [-6.443, -0.396] (P+ 0.0014) DOES sit entirely below zero, but it is built from only 6 blocks (one per season) and is reported here as a secondary, coarser read, not as grounds for a terminal verdict on its own. No positive control was run. This is also explicitly a diagnostic on already-looked-at windows (several of the six overlays were themselves screened or tuned on spans this archive re-touches), continuous evidence rather than a fresh confirmation, so it would not license a terminal closure even if the primary interval had excluded zero.
overlay_stack_combined_opener_2020_2025.description: Joint (OR-combined: flip if ANY overlay's independent condition fires against the SAME baseline pick) application of all six live pick-flipping ACTIVE_PROSPECTIVE overlay challengers atop the active model's own opener-graded picks (production probability rule), 2020-2025, 1537 REG games (1503 non-push, 34 pushes excluded). Baseline accuracy 53.36%, combined-stack accuracy 50.37%. Trigger counts: coach_fade 107, injury_value_lost_tilt 589, division_revenge_tilt 151, backup_qb_fade 181, surface_switch_tilt 239, spread_gap_zone_fade 195 (sum of solo flips 1462, union 1014 games, 365 touched by 2+ overlays). Every overlay's flip equals the complement of the SAME unflipped baseline pick (verified programmatically), so overlap is redundant coverage, never a contradictory recommendation -- zero direction conflicts are possible by construction and zero were found. Per-overlay marginal (leave-one-out) week-blocked deltas: backup_qb_fade_overlay -1.53pts P+0.007; coach_fade_overlay -0.07pts P+0.409; division_revenge_tilt_overlay +0.40pts P+0.755; injury_value_lost_tilt_overlay -2.53pts P+0.023; spread_gap_zone_fade_overlay +0.20pts P+0.617; surface_switch_tilt_overlay -1.00pts P+0.023. Excludes mod07_weak_signal_stack (IS the baseline model itself, not an overlay on top of it) and best_pick_nomination_v2 (never changes home_cover_probability, only which already-picked game gets the Best-Pick marker).

penalty_discipline.description: Team penalty rate, quartile split against the market.
penalty_discipline.notes: Re-measured 2026-08-18 via scripts/penalty_discipline_interval.py (this session); no script behind the original 0.67/49.85%/50.52% numbers survives. RECONSTRUCTION: team penalty rate = mean(penalty) over ALL raw REG-season play-by-play rows (no play-type filter) where posteam==team -- of several definitions tried, the only one reproducing the recorded 0.0750 mean / 0.0101 sd / +0.261 year-over-year reliability (this session's independent reproduction: mean 0.07505, sd 0.01013, reliability +0.2604 on 512 team-season pairs -- reconciles ROADMAP's +0.261 phrasing with the registry's stored 0.261, same figure to 3sf). Global quartile split (pd.qcut, 4 bins) of PRIOR-season (lagged) team penalty rate, joined to REG-season team-games (data/processed/game_features.parquet, pushes dropped since home_cover is undefined for them): least-penalized quartile covers 50.56% (n=2069 team-games), most-penalized covers 49.90% (n=2016) -- both within 0.07 points of the recorded 50.52%/49.85%, raw gap +0.655 vs the recorded +0.67 (within the 0.3-point reconstruction tolerance this session was given). Sample: 4,085 team-game rows / 3,070 unique games in the quartile pair (recorded ~4,431, about 8% higher; per-season quartile cuts, including postseason, and scoring pushes as losses were all tried and reproduced the target LESS well, so were rejected in favour of the construction reported here; no surviving script to check the exact discrepancy against, reported not hidden). SCALE (this entry had a scale bug once before, corrected 2026-08-17): the OLD 0.67 effect field was the UNSCALED quartile-pair gap. Following the hc_year_one_fade precedent (raw subset effect x fraction of slate the subset represents), this entry now records the FULL-SLATE-SCALED effect: 0.655 (raw quartile gap, points) x 0.5020 (fraction of the team-game universe the quartile pair represents, since 2 of 4 quartiles are used) = 0.3288 -- THAT is the new effect value; the raw 0.67/0.655 number is preserved here, not silently dropped. UNCERTAINTY: week-blocked (block id = season*100+week, this project's standard convention, 20,000 resamples, seed 20260818, 277 blocks) 95% [-1.0389, +1.6849], se 0.6938, P+ 0.6828 -- RECORDED as this entry's interval/standard_error/probability_positive. Season-blocked secondary (16 season blocks, same seed/samples): 95% [-0.4527, +1.0654], se 0.3887, P+ 0.7886. Both cross zero; per AGENTS.md this is not grounds for rejection, so classification stays unresolved_below_power -- the direction still favours the candidate hypothesis (68-79 percent of resamples, depending on blocking), just not resolvably. sample_blocks (277) is the week-blocked bootstrap's block count under the season*100+week convention, replacing the prior entry's unsourced 17.

player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.classification_evidence: Reclassified 2026-08-18 from refuted_mechanism. The prior refutation stated the two arms 'differ only in ridge alpha (1 vs 10)'; that is factually wrong about THIS entry, whose arms (candidate, base_alpha1) are BOTH alpha=1 and differ only in feature set (measured: predictions.parquet ridge_alpha is 1.0 for both). The near-null-contrast and 0.03%/0.27% shrinkage argument belongs to the SEPARATE alpha-only contrast base_alpha1 vs base_alpha10, which flips only 25/997 picks (2.51%) and is resolvably negative. This feature contrast flips 177/997 (17.75%), split 94-83, paired SE 1.33 pts, MDE80 3.74 pts. The prior evidence also compared a PAIRED delta against an UNPAIRED coin-flip sd (1.58), overstating noise. The two +-1.1033 figures are independent measurements that cancel by algebraic identity (candidate minus base_alpha10 = 0), not one number explaining the other. No split-half reliability was ever measured for the trait and no family-specific positive control exists, so neither admissible closing ground is met.
player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.description: QB + lineup continuity features, compared at MATCHED regularization (both arms ridge alpha=1); only the feature set differs.
player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.notes: Window [2014, 2017] remains permanently SPENT; only the interpretation of the spent look changes. sample_blocks switched 4 -> 68: the recorded [0.0, 2.2177] was season-blocked on exactly 4 blocks, on the documented degeneracy floor with a lower bound of exactly 0.0. The 68-week-blocked interval on the identical 997 games is the trustworthy one. Actionable reading unchanged and now better supported: the features want less regularization than the rest of the design, which points at group-wise ridge penalties.

proxy_opener_production_rule_2009_2019.classification_evidence: Primary (week-blocked, production probability-rule, pooled 2011-2019 proxy-opener vs 50%) interval [-1.600, +2.370] accuracy points crosses zero with a positive upper bound -- per AGENTS.md this is the EXPECTED shape for a real small signal, not grounds to close. wrong_sign_resolved does not apply (requires the WHOLE interval below zero; this interval's upper bound is positive). No positive-control bound was run, so positive_control_bound does not apply either. The calibration arm's own paired delta (SBR-Open vs true-opener, production rule) is itself unresolved (P+ 0.167, interval crosses zero) so it cannot be used to reclassify this result either. The only admissible classification is unresolved_below_power.
proxy_opener_production_rule_2009_2019.description: Production model (market_residual/weak_stack/ridge alpha=10.0) walked forward week-by-week exactly as nfl_ats.clv.opener_pick_evaluation does, scored with SBR sportsbookreviewsonline.com 'Open' substituted as the settlement/prediction line -- a PROXY for the true Tuesday opener (r=0.949, mean |diff| 1.36-1.37 pts vs the true opener on the only overlap seasons, docs/sbr_odds_archive.md) -- on 11 seasons (2009-2019) the purchased point-in-time market archive cannot reach. 500-game warm-up floor (same constant/mechanism as the rotation registry's rule 9) consumes 2009-2010 entirely; scored population is 2011-2019, 2,304 games, 153 weeks. Reported alongside a same-instrument 2020-2021 dual-grade calibration arm (SBR-Open vs true tue_open, same weekly-refit models, 466 paired games) that measures the proxy discount directly rather than assuming it.
proxy_opener_production_rule_2009_2019.notes: seed=20260817; samples=20000; config=weak_stack/ridge/alpha=10.0 (matches artifacts/active_ats_model.json); min_train_games=500. MAIN ARM: population 2,816/2,816 REG games 2009-2019 have an SBR Open (100% match, 2 flagged open_ambiguous, kept). Warm-up (500-game floor, same mechanism as rotation.py rule 9) consumes 2009-2010 entirely (0 of 34 weeks scorable); 2011-2019 fully scorable. Scored: 2304 games, 153 weeks, seasons 2011-2019. Absolute pooled accuracy: production rule 50.3810%, sign rule 50.4706%. Per-season (sign/production): 2009: warm-up, not scorable; 2010: warm-up, not scorable; 2011: sign 46.80% / prod 45.20%; 2012: sign 50.00% / prod 50.00%; 2013: sign 52.05% / prod 52.46%; 2014: sign 51.78% / prod 51.38%; 2015: sign 49.60% / prod 50.00%; 2016: sign 51.23% / prod 52.87%; 2017: sign 54.03% / prod 52.02%; 2018: sign 49.59% / prod 47.13%; 2019: sign 49.19% / prod 52.42%. Pooled vs 50% coin flip -- PRODUCTION RULE (primary, registered effect is week-blocked): week-blocked estimate=+0.3810 pts, 95% [-1.6001, +2.3702] pts, P+=0.6468; season-blocked estimate=+0.3810 pts, 95% [-1.3671, +1.8652] pts, P+=0.6829. SIGN RULE (secondary, historical protocol comparability): week-blocked estimate=+0.4706 pts, 95% [-1.6577, +2.5986] pts, P+=0.6669; season-blocked estimate=+0.4706 pts, 95% [-0.8057, +1.7457] pts, P+=0.7582. COMPARISON: the 2020-2025 true-opener production-rule figure is 53.36%, season-blocked 95% [51.97%, 54.56%] (docs/opener_evaluation.md, artifacts/opener_evaluation/20260819T174244Z/) -- this run's 2011-2019 proxy-opener pooled production-rule accuracy (50.38%) sits roughly 3 points closer to a coin flip than either the 6-season true-opener figure or the true-opener reading on the identical 2020-2021 seasons measured in the calibration arm (53.73%). CALIBRATION ARM (2020-2021, same weekly-refit models, both grades on the same 466 paired games, mean |line diff|=1.371 pts, reproduces docs/sbr_odds_archive.md's independently-measured 1.36pt figure): absolute accuracy -- SBR-Open sign 54.85%, SBR-Open production 52.86%, true-opener sign 53.29%, true-opener production 53.73%. Paired delta (SBR minus true), production rule (primary): week-blocked estimate=-0.8646 pts, 95% [-2.6218, +0.9074] pts, P+=0.1670 (proxy reads LOWER than true opener under the rule that matters, unresolved). Sign rule: week-blocked estimate=+1.5563 pts, P+=0.8946 (proxy reads HIGHER under this rule -- the two rules disagree on the discount's direction, both unresolved). READING: neither admissible AGENTS.md closing ground applies (whole interval not below zero; no positive control run) -- unresolved_below_power is the only admissible classification. The calibration arm's measured discount (-0.865 pts, itself unresolved) is far too small to explain the ~3-point gap between the proxy-opener 2011-2019 pooled read and the true-opener figures by itself; whether the remaining gap is proxy-instrument noise, era-dependent model edge, or both is NOT resolved by this measurement (inferred discussion only, not claimed as fact). spec/script=scripts/proxy_opener_replication.py; artifact=artifacts/proxy_opener_replication/20260819T194330Z/summary.json; predeclaration=docs/proxy_opener_replication.md.

qb_news_backup_visible_by_deadline_scree.notes: Revives backup_qb_fade_overlay (killed dead-on-arrival in docs/prospective_evidence.md: schedules.parquet QB-name columns are post-game-only) via timestamped PFT (299,739 urls, docs/injury_news_sourcing.md) + PFR-transactions (72,368 urls, docs/pfr_transactions_sourcing.md) news corpora, per owner correction 2026-08-20 that picks are editable up to each game's own deadline = min(kickoff, that week's Sunday 16:00 ET), not just Tuesday noon. Ground truth: 916 backup starts / 4588 eligible (>=3 prior starts) team-games, 2015-2025, identical construct to bias_battery_backup_qb_start. Visibility (matching rule + buckets frozen in docs/qb_news_channel.md before any cover rate was seen; QB full name + a 64-keyword injury/start/bench/roster-move list, both corpora, 10-day lookback anchored on the deadline): 26.31% by Tuesday noon, 39.96% cumulative by Friday, 44.98% cumulative by Sunday 10am ET-or-deadline (this screen's flag), 47.27% cumulative before the deadline, 52.73% never -- vs. the 2.39%-by-Tuesday-noon comparator for the official Wed-Fri injury report alone (docs/injury_news_sourcing.md sec 5.1), an ~11x improvement from using outlet news instead of the mandated report. Flag = backup start AND news-visible by that bucket; complement = every other eligible team-game. Sign=+1 matches bias_battery_backup_qb_start's own convention exactly (comparable without a flip). Comparators: bias_battery_backup_qb_start -0.2731 pts P+0.1684 (close-graded, 2009-2025, 7002 games); bias_battery_backup_qb_start_opener -2.3578 pts P+0.0982 (opener-graded, 2020-2025, 2436 games). This news-visible subset leans the SAME (negative) direction but is MUCH weaker (P+0.39145 vs 0.098-0.168) than the full backup-start population -- my inference, not measured: foreshadowed backups may already be partly priced by the time other bettors see the same news, unlike silent backup starts; not verified here. SNF/MNF deadline correction (owner, 2026-08-20): 313/916 backup-start games had kickoff after that week's Sunday 16:00 ET (258 late-Sunday/SNF, 55 Monday) and were therefore potentially affected; directly measured only 3/916 (0.33%) had their earliest qualifying match actually fall in the [Sunday 16:00 ET, kickoff) gap under a plain-kickoff boundary, so the correction is real but immaterial to the headline number -- applied and re-run anyway (this entry's numbers are the corrected-deadline run, not the plain-kickoff run). Reliability: not_applicable -- like backup_qb_start itself, this is a per-game situational flag (this start's own news timing), not a persistent per-team/per-entity trait; nothing to split-half. Week-blocked (block=season*100+week), 20000 resamples, seed=20260819, full-slate scaling (fraction_of_slate=0.0898) per scripts/nfl_bias_battery_screen.py convention. No rotation-registry window drawn (screen precedent, not a spec-registered family). EV note: another agent is wiring the late-week refresh pipeline; nothing here is wired into any live pick path -- this is measurement only.

surface_familiarity_r1_turf_venue_visito.classification_evidence: An interval or CI that contains zero is NEVER grounds to reject, fail, or close an experiment. At this evaluator's ~2-point resolution, contains zero is the EXPECTED outcome for a real small signal. Only two grounds ever close a line of work: (1) refuted mechanism -- a RESOLVED wrong sign (whole interval on the wrong side of zero) or zero split-half reliability; (2) bounded by a positive control proven able to detect an effect that size. Everything else is unresolved_below_power. Week-blocked 95% CI [-0.477,+3.366] crosses zero -- expected shape, not grounds to close. No admissible closing ground applies: wrong_sign_resolved requires the WHOLE interval on the wrong (negative) side and this interval's upper bound is +3.37 (predicted/positive side); no positive-control bound was run. Follow-up on a mined weather-battery cell (multiplicity already spent upstream), so recorded unresolved_below_power regardless of shape, matching the parent entry's own precedent.
surface_familiarity_r1_turf_venue_visito.description: Venue-controlled follow-up on weather_battery_surface_switch_grass_to_turf (registry), which conflated turf venue with grass-modal visitor. WITHIN turf-venue REG games only (surface_norm=='turf'), grass-modal-home visitor (mismatched, n=1112, home_cover=0.5225) vs turf-modal-home visitor (matched, n=745, home_cover=0.4886); raw gap +3.389pts, fraction_of_slate 0.4302 (n_pair 1857/4317), full-slate effect +1.458pts. Decisive read: the gap survives holding the venue fixed and is LARGER than the original unconditional battery cell's full-slate effect (+1.16pts).
surface_familiarity_r1_turf_venue_visito.notes: Mining lineage: follow-up screen (scripts/surface_familiarity_screen.py) on weather_battery_surface_switch_grass_to_turf, isolating visitor-surface-familiarity from turf-venue by holding venue fixed. season-blocked secondary (17 seasons): 95% [-0.408,+3.355] P+=0.9343, closely matching week-blocked. Franchise-cluster robustness (R4, not a separate registry entry): re-intervaled with a home-franchise-blocked bootstrap (18 franchise blocks) gives 95% [-0.583,+3.752] P+=0.9152 -- comparable width to the week-blocked interval, not dramatically wider, so the effect is not concentrated in one or two outlier franchises, though DET (+2.31pts) and IND (+1.95pts) are the largest positive per-franchise contributors to the raw gap (additive decomposition), partly offset by NE (-1.60pts) and NO (-1.19pts). Era split (R3, separate registry entries) shows the effect roughly 4.5x larger in 2018-2025 (full-slate +2.39pts, P+=0.958) than in 2009-2017 (full-slate +0.53pts, P+=0.648) -- both eras positive-signed but the earlier arm is far weaker. Roof split (R5, report-only): dome/closed full-slate +0.99pts P+=0.916 (n_pair=950) vs outdoor-turf full-slate +0.46pts P+=0.741 (n_pair=907) -- both same-signed, so not purely a dome-noise artifact. Mirror read (R2, separate registry entry) does NOT show the predicted symmetric effect within grass-venue games (P+=0.32). Predeclaration frozen before scoring.

surface_familiarity_r2_grass_venue_mirro.description: Symmetry mirror of R1 on the same lead. WITHIN grass-venue REG games only (surface_norm=='grass'), turf-modal-home visitor (mismatched, n=1114, home_cover=0.4704) vs grass-modal-home visitor (matched, n=1304, home_cover=0.4793); raw gap -0.892pts (wrong-direction point estimate: home_cover is LOWER, not higher, against a mismatched turf-modal visitor), fraction_of_slate 0.5601 (n_pair 2418/4317), full-slate effect -0.4995pts. A true bilateral visitor-surface-familiarity mechanism predicts a POSITIVE gap here, symmetric to R1; this read does not corroborate that.
surface_familiarity_r2_grass_venue_mirro.notes: Mining lineage: mirror follow-up on weather_battery_surface_switch_grass_to_turf via scripts/surface_familiarity_screen.py, testing whether a turf-modal visitor on grass underperforms a matched grass-modal visitor (symmetric to R1's turf-venue read). season-blocked secondary (17 seasons): 95% [-3.173,+2.247] P+=0.3524, consistent with week-blocked. This is the read that most argues against a clean bilateral familiarity mechanism: R1 (turf venue) shows P+=0.933 in the predicted direction while R2 (grass venue) shows P+=0.320, near a coin flip and slightly favoring the wrong sign. Read together, R1+R2 is more consistent with something turf-venue-specific than with a symmetric surface-switch-cost mechanism that should fire in both directions equally. Predeclaration frozen before scoring.
